title: BI-DIRECTIONAL BIAS ATTRIBUTION: DEBIASING LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS WITHOUT MODIFYING PROMPTS
findings: The proposed debiasing methods, Forward Bias Attribution (FBA) and Backward Bias Attribution (BBA), effectively reduce stereotypical bias related to religion in the tested LLMs (Llama-3.1, Llama-3.2, Mistral-v0.3). On the StereoSet benchmark, these methods brought the stereotype score (SS) for the religion domain closer to the ideal 50% fairness mark and significantly improved the overall ICAT fairness metric, outperforming other baseline debiasing techniques without a substantial loss in language modeling capability.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured stereotypical bias in religious contexts. Specifically, it assessed whether language models favor stereotypical content over unbiased or unrelated alternatives when presented with prompts related to religion, using datasets like StereoSet and BBQ.
